nodes.norm_label: longest-path rank for nodes without an explicit column hint.

nodes.label: (cx, cy, left, right, top, bottom, column) for a node OR group id.
nodes.norm_label: (cx, cy, left, right, top, bottom, column) for a node or group id.

nodes.label: Orthogonal routing: adjacent columns via gutter lanes; same-column     via short
nodes.norm_label: orthogonal routing: adjacent columns via gutter lanes; same-column     via short

nodes.label: Tech Stack
nodes.rationale: Canvas 2D drawn by hand because per-node radial gradients and zoom level-of-detail are the signature visuals a graph library would fight; d3-force layout runs offline at build time so the map is identical on every visit and spatial memory works.

nodes.label: Pure Logic Is Tested; Rendering Is Not
nodes.rationale: Anything deciding WHAT appears on screen is a pure unit-tested function kept out of the render loop; canvas drawing code is verified by looking at it. E2E canvas tests would mostly assert that pixels were painted.
nodes.norm_label: pure logic is tested; rendering is not

nodes.label: The Shape of the System
nodes.rationale: Two halves that never talk at runtime: MusicBrainz 1 req/s and Deezer 50 req/5s make per-visitor API calls impossible, and the static split means the site cannot break because an upstream service is down.

nodes.label: Stage 2 Is the Fragile One (HTML scraping)
nodes.rationale: MusicBrainz genre-to-genre relations are not in the JSON API (inc=genre-rels silently returns nothing, verified 2026-08-04); the data exists only on HTML pages and the 7 GB dump, so the pipeline scrapes 2,184 genre pages with fixture-tested parsing.
nodes.norm_label: stage 2 is the fragile one (html scraping)

nodes.label: Stage 3 Threshold Filter
nodes.rationale: About 40% of MusicBrainz genres cannot fill a detail panel (acholitronix: zero tagged release-groups vs rock: 547,091); the threshold filter keeps empty nodes off the map, and five-orders-of-magnitude popularity forces logarithmic radius scaling.

nodes.label: The Three Rules That Define the Interaction
nodes.norm_label: the three rules that define the interaction

nodes.label: Rule 1: Edges - only subgenre-of drawn
nodes.rationale: Only subgenre-of edges are drawn, one parent per node; fusion-of and influenced-by stay in the dataset and affect focus only. MusicBrainz models exactly this structural/associative split, a large part of why it was chosen.

nodes.label: Rule 3: Colour - family hue, depth gradient
nodes.norm_label: rule 3: colour - family hue, depth gradient

nodes.label: Camera Model
nodes.rationale: Baked d3-force positions are the resting state; the focus fan is a rendering transform only. The map you learn must be the map you get - that is why layout is offline and no live simulation runs in the browser.

nodes.label: Auth Model - no accounts, no server
nodes.rationale: No accounts, no server, no API keys: every upstream source is open and unauthenticated; the only credential is the GITHUB_TOKEN the refresh workflow uses to open a PR. A static site cannot hold a secret.
nodes.norm_label: auth model - no accounts, no server

nodes.label: Committed Dataset Artifact
nodes.rationale: public/data/ is checked into the repo, produced only by the pipeline and refreshed only via PR - the dataset goes through the same review gate as code, never hand-edited.

nodes.label: Personal Lens - Scoped Runtime Network Exception
nodes.rationale: The one exception to build-time-only network calls: src/personal/ may call api.listenbrainz.org, user-initiated only, degrading to 'feature unavailable'; the map itself never depends on it.
nodes.norm_label: personal lens - scoped runtime network exception

nodes.label: Workflow (local guidance, revised 2026-07-22)
nodes.rationale: Owner verdict after a side-by-side comparison: hand-tuned layout produces the better diagram - denser packing and short labeled connections beat the auto-router's channel detours. Manual layout is primary; auto-layout output is a draft scaffold only.

nodes.label: CI verify job - lint, format, typecheck, test, build
nodes.rationale: Wired as a required status check on main so a red run blocks the merge button; also reports bundle and graph.json size so the payload budget stays visible in the run summary.
nodes.norm_label: ci verify job - lint, format, typecheck, test, build

nodes.label: Deploy Site Workflow (deploy-pages.yml)
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages became the host the moment the repo went public (2026-08-08) - its only disqualifier in the hosting research was that private repos need a paid plan; Cloudflare Pages remains the documented fallback.

nodes.label: SPA Fallback via 404.html
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages serves 404.html for unknown paths; copying index.html there makes deep links like /genre-explorer/genre/house load the app, which reads the real path from the address bar.

nodes.label: Refresh Dataset Workflow (refresh-data.yml)
nodes.rationale: Rebuilds public/data/ weekly (Sundays 04:00 UTC, when MusicBrainz is quietest) and opens a PR - never pushes to main, so the sharp-drop guard and CI review every refresh.

nodes.label: refresh job - rebuild and open PR
nodes.norm_label: refresh job - rebuild and open pr

nodes.label: Prune Volatile Cache step (scheduled runs)
nodes.rationale: A refresh that reuses last week's scrape refreshes nothing: scheduled runs drop the volatile cache (tree, counts, searches, rankings) but keep stable id mappings (streaming links, Deezer ids) so a steady-state run fits in ~2.5-3 h; a manual dispatch after a timeout must resume, not restart.

nodes.label: Actions Cache as Cross-Run Resume
nodes.rationale: A fully cold build (~9 h) exceeds the 6-hour job limit; the pipeline's disk cache is saved to the Actions cache even when the job fails or times out (per-run key + prefix restore-keys), so a rerun continues where the last one stopped.

nodes.label: Notable Constraint: Spotify Is a Link Target, Not a Data Source
nodes.rationale: As of Feb 2026 the Spotify Web API removed artist-top-tracks/browse/batch endpoints, capped search at 10, requires the owner to hold Premium, allows 5 dev-mode users, and grants extended quota only to 250k+ MAU orgs - so Spotify appears purely as an outbound link, sourced from MusicBrainz.
nodes.norm_label: notable constraint: spotify is a link target, not a data source

nodes.label: Tech Stack (choices and rejections)
nodes.rationale: Each layer chosen with rejected alternatives on record: MusicBrainz over Every Noise (frozen, no hierarchy) and Wikidata (no popularity signal); Canvas 2D over Sigma.js (gradients need custom GLSL) and react-force-graph (re-simulates per load); offline d3-force over live simulation (spatial memory); TS pipeline over Python (shared types fail tsc on both sides); Zod over hand-written guards.

nodes.label: The Hard Part - genre hierarchy extraction
nodes.rationale: MusicBrainz has the tree but the JSON API does not expose it (inc=genre-rels silently empty, verified 2026-08-04). Chosen route: scrape 2,184 genre HTML pages at 1 req/s (~37 min, cached, refreshed weekly) over the 7 GB mbdump Postgres import; the scraper is isolated with fixture tests and the build fails loudly on sharp edge-count drops.
nodes.norm_label: the hard part - genre hierarchy extraction

nodes.label: MusicBrainz
nodes.rationale: The only open source with a real genre tree; its structural/associative relationship split matches the project's edge rules exactly. 1 req/s rate limit, User-Agent with contact info required, core data CC0.

nodes.label: ListenBrainz
nodes.rationale: Real listen counts, free and unauthenticated; the spread (5.2M listens down to 1) cleanly separates popular from obscure. Documented GET popularity endpoints return 500, so the pipeline uses the POST endpoints.

nodes.label: Deezer
nodes.rationale: 30-second preview MP3s with no API key at 50 req/5s; preview URLs expire in ~12 min so the dataset stores stable track ids and embeds the widget player.

nodes.label: Spotify (outbound link target only)
nodes.rationale: Not a data source: Feb 2026 API removals (artist-top-tracks, browse, batch), a 10-result search cap, the Premium requirement, 5 dev-mode users, and the 250k-MAU extended-quota bar make it unusable; links come from MusicBrainz URL relationships instead.

nodes.label: Every Noise at Once
nodes.rationale: Not used as a source - frozen since Dec 2023 with similarity coordinates but no hierarchy - but the inspiration for the whole idea.

nodes.label: Canvas 2D + d3-zoom Rendering (chosen)
nodes.rationale: Chosen because per-node radial gradients are one line of ctx.createRadialGradient, LOD is a plain if in the draw loop, d3-zoom gives wheel/pan/animated fly-to for free, and 1,200 nodes render at 60fps on 2D canvas so WebGL buys nothing. Accepted cost: hand-written hit-testing, label collision and render loop.

nodes.label: Sigma.js v3 (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: per-node gradient fill would require custom GLSL WebGL node programs, making the signature visual the hardest code in the repo; its 10k+ node performance advantage is irrelevant at ~1,200 nodes. Worth revisiting past ~10k nodes.

nodes.label: react-force-graph (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: runs the force simulation live in the browser so the layout differs on every visit, breaking spatial memory; weakest styling and LOD control of the candidates.

nodes.label: Cytoscape.js (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected: DOM-dependent, single-threaded, CSS-like styling model; aimed at network analysis, not a designed visual experience.

nodes.label: Offline d3-force Layout (build-time baked coordinates)
nodes.rationale: Layout computed once at build time by d3-force in Node, x/y baked into the dataset JSON: the map is identical on every visit and device, the browser never runs a simulation, and first paint is immediate — spatial memory is the product requirement.

nodes.label: Force Constellation with Radial Focus Mode
nodes.rationale: Pure force layout leaves dense families tangled; pure radial tree reads as an org chart and mishandles fusion genres. Chosen hybrid: baked force positions as resting state, children animate onto a ring on click — purely a rendering transform, data unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: force constellation with radial focus mode

nodes.label: Zoom Level of Detail (lod.ts rules)
nodes.rationale: Node visibility decided by zoom vs popularity cutoff, focus subtree override, and filter selection; labels have a stricter threshold than dots. Kept pure in src/graph/lod.ts with unit tests because the rule is easy to get subtly wrong and impossible to eyeball.

nodes.label: Fusion Edge Rule (structural drawn, associative hidden)
nodes.rationale: Only 'subgenre of' edges are drawn; 'fusion of' and 'influenced by' stay in the dataset and only affect focus reveal, so a fusion genre like alternative dance appears under both parents when each is focused without either edge ever being drawn. Pure and unit-tested in src/graph/edges.ts.
nodes.norm_label: fusion edge rule (structural drawn, associative hidden)

nodes.label: Cloudflare Pages (chosen host)
nodes.rationale: Chosen for unlimited free bandwidth on static assets (dataset JSON is the bulk of the payload and served to every visitor) plus private-repo deploys and 500 builds/month; Netlify and Vercel cap at 100 GB/month.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages Disqualification (private repo)
nodes.rationale: Disqualified outright at research time: serving Pages from a private repo requires a paid GitHub plan — the deciding constraint before any performance comparison. Later reversed when the repo went public on 2026-08-08.

nodes.label: graph.json / genres per-id Payload Split
nodes.rationale: Full dataset is 3-6 MB uncompressed — too much to block first paint. Split: graph.json (nodes + structural edges, under 400 KB) paints the map; genres/<id>.json fetched lazily on focus and cached. Recorded as architecture, not later optimisation, because retrofitting would rewrite both build script and loader.

nodes.label: ListenBrainz Bridge Intake
nodes.rationale: Recommended public intake: users link Spotify once in ListenBrainz; its stats API is keyless, CORS *, and returns artist_mbid values matching the pipeline's Artist.mbid exactly — no fuzzy matching. Caveat verified live: stats are precomputed, can 204, and the batch pipeline can lag by weeks, hence the raw-listens fallback.

nodes.label: Spotify OAuth Personal Mode (<=5 users)
nodes.rationale: Technically alive (GET /me/top and recently-played survived Feb 2026; PKCE needs no secret so a static site can run the flow) but practically closed: dev mode caps at 5 manually-allowlisted users and extended quota requires a 250k+ MAU registered organization. Viable only as a hidden owner mode, never the public story.

nodes.label: Spotify GDPR Export Upload (offline fallback)
nodes.rationale: Drag-and-drop of Spotify's extended streaming history ZIP, parsed entirely in the browser — zero network, nothing uploaded. Lossier (no MBIDs, name matching only, up to ~30-day delivery delay); a v2 addition behind the same (artistKey, weight)[] interface.

nodes.label: Artist to Genre Reverse Index (artist-index.json)
nodes.rationale: The missing artifact: runtime data is keyed genre-to-artists, so a new build-time emit inverts stage 4's existing 50-candidates-per-genre into public/data/artist-index.json keyed by MBID with normalized names. Lazy-loaded only when the feature activates, so graph.json keeps its 400 KB budget. Coverage honest by construction: artists outside every top-50 simply don't light up.

nodes.label: Branch-out Adjacency Scoring
nodes.rationale: Genre suggestions need no external API: graph.json already ships every subgenre/fusion/influence edge, and a pure unit-testable function scores unlistened genres by adjacency (fusion/influence being the strongest 'sounds adjacent' signal). Replaces Spotify's removed /recommendations endpoint with data every visitor already has.

nodes.label: localStorage Persistence, No Accounts
nodes.rationale: Accounts are unnecessary: the personal subgraph lives in localStorage — no login, no server, no secrets, clearable in one click. A static site cannot hold a secret and this design never asks it to; Cloudflare Worker + KV only if cross-device sync ever becomes real demand.

nodes.label: Scoped Runtime Network Exception
nodes.rationale: The 'network calls at build time only' rule gains exactly one carve-out: api.listenbrainz.org from the browser, only on explicit user action, degrading to 'feature unavailable' — the map itself never depends on it. Personal data is a highlight/dim lens like the filter panel, never a layout change.

nodes.label: Spotify API Deprecation (2024-2026)
nodes.rationale: The finding that shaped the project: Nov 2024 removed recommendations/audio-features/related-artists/preview_url for new apps; Feb 2026 removed top-tracks, browse and batch endpoints for everyone, cut search limit 50 to 10, and locked extended quota to 250k+ MAU organizations. Spotify survives only as outbound open.spotify.com links.

nodes.label: Every Noise at Once (rejected prior art)
nodes.rationale: Frozen since McDonald's Dec 2023 layoff, derived from scraped Spotify data of murky licensing, and — decisively — has no hierarchy, only 2D similarity coordinates. The entire product is the tree. Useful only as naming inspiration and cross-check.
nodes.norm_label: every noise at once (rejected prior art)

nodes.label: MusicBrainz Data Backbone
nodes.rationale: The discovery that makes the project buildable: 2,184 genres with subgenre-of / fusion-of / influenced-by relationships matching the plan's edge model one-to-one, artist tag search per genre, and url-rels handing over canonical Spotify/SoundCloud/Bandcamp links from a CC0 database without touching the Spotify API.

nodes.label: Genre HTML Page Scrape (relations absent from JSON API)
nodes.rationale: The silent failure mode: inc=genre-rels returns 200 OK with relations absent, so genre relationships exist only on HTML pages and in the 7 GB database dump. Chosen: scrape the 2,184 genre pages at MusicBrainz's 1 req/s (~37 min one-time), disk-cached, with the dump documented as fallback if the HTML layout changes.
nodes.norm_label: genre html page scrape (relations absent from json api)

nodes.label: ListenBrainz Popularity API
nodes.rationale: Free unauthenticated listen counts drive the popular/obscure split: rank candidates by total_listen_count, top 5 popular, 5 from a defined tail band (not the absolute bottom — 1-listen recordings are data artifacts). The documented GET convenience endpoints 500'd, so the pipeline uses tag search + bulk POST /popularity/* instead.

nodes.label: Deezer Preview MP3s
nodes.rationale: Public API, no key, 50 req/5s: used for one job only — resolving a 30-second preview per track. No Deezer match means the preview button is absent; previews degrade, they don't break the panel.

nodes.label: Genre Data Threshold Filter
nodes.rationale: Release-group counts span five orders of magnitude (rock 547,091 vs acholitronix 0), so node radius must be log-scaled and the long tail is genuinely empty — a node opening an empty panel breaks the core promise, hence filtering 2,184 genres down to those clearing a data threshold (settled at 50 release-groups, keeping 912).

nodes.label: verify CI Gate
nodes.rationale: One job in .github/workflows/ci.yml running npm ci, lint, format:check, typecheck, test, build on every PR and push to main; npm run verify is the identical local sequence. required_approving_review_count is 0 on purpose — solo project, a self-unapprovable review would make main unreachable.

nodes.label: protect-main.sh Local Hook
nodes.rationale: PreToolUse hook denying git commit/merge/push against main from inside Claude Code sessions — covers the accident-in-the-moment case and works even with no server-side protection.

nodes.label: Server-side Branch Protection on main
nodes.rationale: GitHub rule requiring PR, green 'verify' check, strict up-to-date branch, resolved conversations, admins enforced. Initially NOT active: 403 on private repos under a free plan (verified 2026-08-04), leaving the local hook as the only guard and red CI unable to block merges — the gap later closed by making the repo public.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages Deployment
nodes.rationale: Live at aakash-tir.github.io/genre-explorer via deploy-pages.yml on every merge to main. Going public on 2026-08-08 removed GitHub Pages' only disqualifier from the hosting research. Builds with --base=/genre-explorer/, resolves data URLs and deep links against BASE_URL, and ships 404.html as the SPA fallback for deep links. No secrets: workflow builds on GITHUB_TOKEN.

nodes.label: Cloudflare Pages Fallback
nodes.rationale: Kept as the documented fallback for its unlimited static bandwidth if traffic ever threatens GitHub Pages' ~100 GB/month soft cap; one-time manual dashboard connection by the repo owner.

nodes.label: Log 2026-08-04: Plan Expansion and Data Research
nodes.norm_label: log 2026-08-04: plan expansion and data research

nodes.label: Disk-cached Resumable Pipeline
nodes.rationale: A previous ~80-minute scrape died mid-way in an internet outage leaving nothing on disk; the rebuilt pipeline disk-caches every response under .cache/build-dataset/ so any interruption resumes instead of restarting — the cache IS the resume mechanism.

nodes.label: Sharp-drop Guard on Emit
nodes.rationale: Emit fails the build if edge counts drop sharply against the committed dataset — the guard against an error page or MusicBrainz redesign parsing as 'genre with no relations' and silently emptying the map.

nodes.label: PR #4 Red Merge Incident
nodes.rationale: PR #4 merged with failing CI: piping gh pr checks --watch to tail made the chain's exit status tail's success, and main had no server-side protection (paid feature on private repos), so nothing blocked the red merge. Fixed by reading gh pr checks' own exit code; structural fix was making the repo public.

nodes.label: Deezer Track ID Pivot (expiring preview URLs)
nodes.rationale: The plan's assumption that Deezer preview MP3 URLs could be baked into the dataset was wrong: verified live, URLs carry an hdnea token expiring in ~12 minutes and the bare URL 403s. The dataset stores the stable Deezer track ID instead (Track.previewUrl -> Track.deezerId, enforced by tsc on both sides) and the panel embeds Deezer's widget on demand. Stage 6 also purges Deezer's HTTP-200 quota-error responses from cache.
nodes.norm_label: deezer track id pivot (expiring preview urls)

nodes.label: Golden-angle Family Hues
nodes.rationale: Hash-based familyHue put rock and electronic at near-identical hues (found live in milestone 3). Replaced by assignFamilyHues: multi-node families ranked by total popularity around the golden angle, singletons sharing a muted neutral, regression-tested that rock and electronic sit >60 degrees apart.

nodes.label: Weekly Refresh Cache Strategy
nodes.rationale: The real pipeline is ~9h cold, over the 6-hour Actions job limit. Made viable by storing the disk cache in the Actions cache with per-run keys persisting across failures (a timed-out run resumes next dispatch), and by pruning only volatile cache directories on scheduled runs while keeping ~10k stable id mappings — cutting a steady-state weekly run to ~2.5-3h.

nodes.label: Constellation UI Overhaul
nodes.rationale: Owner rejected the v1 map (random specks, overlapping nodes, buried focus ring). Rebuilt: family anchors on a golden-angle ring matching the hue wheel, singletons on an outer halo (closing the singleton-placement question), 2.2x collision radii, dust motes below the LOD cutoff, radius growth cut to zoom^0.35, greedy priority label placement (labels.ts), focus dims unrelated nodes to 12% and displaces bystanders outside the fan ring.

nodes.label: Log 2026-08-08: Sticky Selection and Going Public
nodes.norm_label: log 2026-08-08: sticky selection and going public

nodes.label: Sticky Selection (selection vs fan split)
nodes.rationale: Focus split into SELECTION (panel genre, focusId, in the URL) and FAN (ephemeral exploration view) because empty-space clicks while panning were unmounting the Deezer widget mid-song. Empty-space clicks now collapse only the fan; the selection, its panel and playing preview persist until a different genre is clicked.

nodes.label: Repo Went Public + Real Branch Protection + Pages Ship
nodes.rationale: After a full 44-revision history leak sweep (clean; one accepted finding: personal email in 25 commits' author metadata), going public unlocked the two paid-only-on-private features at once: server-side branch protection (closing the red-CI-can-merge gap exploited in PR #4) and GitHub Pages hosting, which unlike Cloudflare needs no manual dashboard step.
nodes.norm_label: repo went public + real branch protection + pages ship

nodes.label: Log 2026-08-10: Docs Sweep and Personal Lens
nodes.norm_label: log 2026-08-10: docs sweep and personal lens

nodes.label: Personal Lens: Spotify Owner Mode Build
nodes.rationale: Built per the owner's decision ('do this for the 1-5 users for now'): client-side OAuth PKCE against the owner's dev-mode app (scope user-top-read only), pure match.ts (spotify-id exact, unambiguous-name fallback — a wrong highlight is worse than a missing one) and suggest.ts, localStorage persistence, map lens with rings/dashed rings/dimming, plus pipeline stage 9 emitting artist-index.json (6,548 artists). Removed on 2026-08-12.
nodes.norm_label: personal lens: spotify owner mode build

nodes.label: Personal Lens: ListenBrainz Public Intake
nodes.rationale: The public path built the same day: any visitor types a ListenBrainz username — no cap, no key, no OAuth. ArtistIndexEntry gained mbid so matching is MusicBrainz-id exact (better than the Spotify path); match.ts generalized to source-agnostic ListenedArtist with mbid > spotifyId > unambiguous-name priority; 204/404 handled as guidance, not errors.

nodes.label: Fixture: acholitronix MusicBrainz genre page
nodes.rationale: Saved real MusicBrainz page for the parser tests; represents the empty long tail — a real genre with zero tagged release-groups, the direct evidence behind the threshold filter.

nodes.label: Fixture: alternative dance MusicBrainz genre page
nodes.rationale: Saved real MusicBrainz page for the parser tests; the canonical fusion-genre case (fusion of alternative rock and dance) exercising the fusion-edge rule.
nodes.norm_label: fixture: alternative dance musicbrainz genre page

nodes.label: Fixture: dubstep MusicBrainz genre page
nodes.rationale: Saved real MusicBrainz page for the parser fixture tests over the genre-to-genre relationship sections.

nodes.label: Fixture: grunge MusicBrainz genre page
nodes.rationale: Saved real MusicBrainz page for the parser tests; demonstrates the plain subgenre-of relationship (grunge is a subgenre of alternative rock).

nodes.label: Deferred from v1
nodes.rationale: Features consciously cut from v1, not forgotten: a client-side Spotify GDPR-export ZIP intake (slots behind the same ListenedArtist[] interface the matcher already uses, so no new matching path), wider artist-index coverage beyond the ~6.5k panel artists, similarity edges, accounts, playlist export, artist/track nodes, a timeline view, and a toggleable influenced-by layer.

nodes.label: Known Gaps (backlog)
nodes.rationale: Accepted shortfalls with their evidence: song rows link to Spotify by search rather than exact track page (2026-08-12); ~28% of ranked tracks have no Deezer match so no preview; Deezer preview URLs expire in ~12 min so the widget player is embedded by stable track id instead; touch untested on a real device; no end-to-end browser tests in v1; hosting is GitHub Pages with Cloudflare Pages the documented fallback; the first scheduled refresh may time out on a cold Actions cache.

nodes.label: Decisions Still Open
nodes.rationale: Calls deliberately left to settle with use: the 100-listen OBSCURE_MIN_LISTENS floor; popular-artist lists skewing to megastars because ranking uses TOTAL artist listens and ListenBrainz exposes no genre-scoped counts (mitigations would be heuristic); and whether the release-group threshold (912 of 2,184 kept) leaves non-Western genre families looking thin.

nodes.label: Upstream Watch
nodes.rationale: Third-party defects the project routes around and would drop if fixed: ListenBrainz's documented GET top-recordings/top-release-groups endpoints return 500 (pipeline uses POST instead), MusicBrainz's JSON API accepts inc=genre-rels but returns nothing (forcing the HTML scraper), and MusicBrainz HTML layout changes will break the stage 2 parser (fixture tests catch it; the 7 GB mbdump import is the fallback).

nodes.label: Scaling
nodes.rationale: Two thresholds that would force a rewrite: past ~10k nodes revisit Canvas 2D vs. Sigma.js/WebGL (at 800-1,200 nodes Canvas is faster to develop against), and graph.json must stay under ~400 KB pre-gzip or be split by genre family and loaded on demand.

nodes.label: No Free Route to an Exact Spotify Track URL
nodes.rationale: Recorded 2026-08-12 as a known gap. Two free routes were probed live and both failed: MusicBrainz recording?inc=url-rels returned zero URL relations for four real dataset tracks (artist-level coverage ~68%, recording-level ~0), and Odesli/song.link resolves a Deezer track to Amazon/Tidal/Napster/Anghami/Boomplay/Yandex but omits Spotify from its unauthenticated tier, confirmed against a global #1 single. An exact link would need Spotify's authenticated API, i.e. a client secret in the pipeline, which the no-keys rule forbids. Deezer links ARE exact because stage 6 already holds the track id. Revisit only if the no-keys rule changes.
nodes.norm_label: no free route to an exact spotify track url

nodes.label: The Big Picture
nodes.rationale: Two halves that never talk at runtime: a build-time pipeline that calls MusicBrainz/ListenBrainz/Deezer and commits static JSON, and a browser that loads only that JSON. Forced by upstream rate limits (MusicBrainz 1 req/s, Deezer 50 per 5 s) which make per-visitor API calls impossible, with the side benefit that an upstream outage cannot take the site down. One scoped exception: the user-initiated personal lens.

nodes.label: The Dataset (public/data/)
nodes.rationale: Three files Zod-validated twice - on emit and on load - so a corrupted weekly refresh fails loudly instead of rendering a subtly wrong map. Schemas live in src/types.ts and are imported by both pipeline and app, so a shape change breaks tsc on both sides at once; that shared compile is the mechanism keeping them in sync.

nodes.label: graph.json - everything needed to paint the map
nodes.rationale: Kept under ~400 KB pre-gzip so it never blocks first paint. Popularity spans five orders of magnitude (rock 547,091 vs vaporwave 15,981), which is why every visual scale is logarithmic; x/y are baked d3-force coordinates so the browser never simulates and the map is pixel-identical on every visit, preserving spatial memory.
nodes.norm_label: graph.json - everything needed to paint the map

nodes.label: genres/<id>.json - per-genre detail files
nodes.rationale: One lazy-loaded file per genre with four lists of five (popular/small artists, popular/obscure tracks), each carrying listen counts, MusicBrainz-derived outbound links, and for tracks an optional deezerId. It stores a stable Deezer track id and NOT a preview URL, because Deezer preview MP3 links carry an auth token expiring in ~12 minutes - a URL baked into a committed dataset would be dead before it merged.

nodes.label: artist-index.json - the personal lens's reverse index
nodes.rationale: Artist to genres, inverted from the detail files at build time. Genre references are integer indexes into a shared genreIds table to keep the payload small, and the file loads only when a listening profile exists, so visitors who never touch the personal lens never pay for it. spotifyId is extracted from the artist's Spotify link (~68% coverage).
nodes.norm_label: artist-index.json - the personal lens's reverse index

nodes.label: The Build Pipeline (scripts/build-dataset/)
nodes.rationale: Eight stages with every HTTP response disk-cached under .cache/build-dataset/, so a cold run is hours, a rerun is seconds, and an interrupted run resumes. Stage 2 scrapes 2,184 MusicBrainz HTML pages at 1 req/s because inc=genre-rels silently returns nothing; stage 3 drops genres below MIN_RELEASE_GROUPS = 50 (912 of 2,184 survive); stage 4 over-fetches at SEARCH_LIMIT = 50 because many recordings have no ListenBrainz data; stage 7 uses a fixed seed and tick count so layout is deterministic.

nodes.label: Sharp-Drop Guard
nodes.rationale: Stage 8 fails the build if node or edge counts fall more than MAX_SHRINK_RATIO = 0.2 against the committed dataset. It exists because the scariest failure is silent: a MusicBrainz HTML change that empties the scraper still emits a valid, nearly treeless dataset that Zod validation alone would happily pass.

nodes.label: Shell and State (App.tsx, deepLink.ts)
nodes.rationale: App state is exactly {focusId, selectedIds, zoom} and the URL IS that state, rewritten via history.replaceState so every view is shareable; deepLink.ts does the pure, sanitised, never-throwing string-object conversion so a mangled URL degrades to the overview. fanOpen is deliberately kept out of the URL: selection stays sticky so a playing preview survives while the map is browsed mid-listen. All URLs resolve against Vite's BASE_URL because GitHub Pages serves under /genre-explorer/.

nodes.label: Loading (src/lib/dataset.ts)
nodes.rationale: createDetailCache caches in-flight promises rather than just results, because double-clicking a node must not fire two requests, and evicts failures, because a transient network blip must not make a genre permanently unopenable.

nodes.label: Camera (src/graph/camera.ts)
nodes.rationale: FIT (world bounding box into the viewport, recomputed per canvas size) composes with the live d3-zoom transform. Keeping them separate is why ?zoom=8 in a shared URL means the same thing on a phone and a desktop: the URL stores the user's zoom factor, never pixel offsets, and zoom 1 always means 'the whole map'.

nodes.label: Level of Detail (src/graph/lod.ts)
nodes.rationale: Visibility is three pure inputs: a zoom cutoff in log10 space falling linearly with log2(zoom) from ~10^4.3 at zoom 1 to 0 at FULL_DETAIL_ZOOM = 64; focus (a focused genre and its children always visible); and filter as a hard gate overriding even focus. Labels are stricter than dots (LABEL_ZOOM_MULTIPLIER = 2) so a genre can be a visible speck before it earns a name, except focused nodes and depth-0 family roots, which are the landmarks the map is navigated by.

nodes.label: The Edge Rule (src/graph/edges.ts)
nodes.rationale: Only subgenre edges are drawn and each genre has at most one drawn parent, so the map is a tree. fusion and influence are associative: never rendered, but focusChildren includes associative children, so alternative dance appears under both alternative rock and dance when each is focused in turn without an edge between the families ever appearing. structuralDescendants follows drawn edges only and is cycle-safe because MusicBrainz is user-edited.

nodes.label: Colour (src/graph/colors.ts)
nodes.rationale: Family hues come from popularity rank around the golden-angle sequence (137.508 degrees), not a name hash - hashing put rock and electronic on nearly the same magenta - and ties break on id so a refresh keeps its colours. The 131 singleton family roots (of 179) share one muted slate-violet neutral rather than burning 131 indistinguishable hues. Depth desaturates and lightens to MAX_RAMP_DEPTH = 4 so distance from the root is readable without labels, and edges drawn in the child's colour at 28% alpha make lines read as lineage.

nodes.label: Focus Fan and Labels (fan.ts, labels.ts)
nodes.rationale: The fan is a rendering transform only - an override map of positions, never a mutation of the baked layout - so releasing focus animates everything back. Ring radius is the larger of clearance around the focused node and the circumference the children need without overlapping; unrelated nodes inside the ring are displaced just outside it while focus is held. labels.ts places earned labels greedily by priority and drops any that would overlap a claimed rectangle, so a dropped label reappears as soon as the camera gives it room.

nodes.label: Rendering (GraphCanvas.tsx)
nodes.rationale: A single imperative Canvas 2D component React does not re-render per frame; it subscribes to d3-zoom once and calls the pure modules each frame. Deliberately not a graph library: per-node radial gradients and zoom LOD are the signature visuals, and Sigma.js (WebGL/GLSL) or react-force-graph (re-simulates every load) would fight exactly those.

nodes.label: Detail Panel (DetailPanel.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Lazy-loads the focused genre's detail file through the session cache and renders four lists with listen counts formatted as magnitude signals ('1.2M', '90k'). One preview plays at a time via Deezer's widget player, embedded on demand by track id. Artist links come from the dataset; song links are derived at render time. Explicit states include loaded-but-thin, a real condition because a genre can clear the release-group threshold yet have no ranked listens.

nodes.label: Derived Song Links (trackLinks.ts)
nodes.rationale: Track.links ships empty because MusicBrainz records streaming URLs on artists but effectively never on recordings, so song links are computed at render time by src/lib/trackLinks.ts instead of being baked. Each song gets a Spotify SEARCH deep link - no key, no fetch, every track covered, and the song is normally the first hit - plus its exact Deezer page when stage 6 resolved an id. Any real link the dataset later carries wins over the derived one, so a future pipeline that bakes track links takes over silently.

nodes.label: Filter Panel (FilterPanel.tsx)
nodes.rationale: Search by name plus multi-select feeding resolveFilter: the map keeps the selected genres and their structural descendants and hides everything else.

nodes.label: The Personal Lens (src/personal/)
nodes.rationale: The one scoped exception to 'no runtime network calls': user-initiated, degrading to 'feature unavailable', and the map never depends on it. Now a single intake path (ListenBrainz username, public CORS-* stats API) reducing to ListenedArtist[], with a raw-listens fallback because the stats batch pipeline can lag weeks. Matching is MBID, then Spotify id, then normalized name only when unique in the index, because crediting the wrong 'Bush' is worse than missing one; matched artists contribute 1/sqrt(rank+1) so the top dominates without the tail vanishing. Suggestions come only from edges already in graph.json (fusion/influence 1, tree 0.7, siblings 0.35) - no external recommendation API.

nodes.label: Automation (.github/workflows/)
nodes.rationale: ci.yml is a required status check mirroring npm run verify; deploy-pages.yml builds with --base=/genre-explorer/ and copies index.html to 404.html as the SPA fallback that makes deep links work on GitHub Pages; refresh-data.yml opens a PR rather than pushing to main so the sharp-drop guard and CI review every refresh. A cold build (~9 h) exceeds the 6-hour job limit, so the disk cache doubles as a cross-run resume mechanism and scheduled runs prune only the volatile cache while keeping stable id mappings.

nodes.label: Testing
nodes.rationale: Pure logic is unit-tested; rendering is not. Everything deciding WHAT appears (edges, lod, colors, fan, labels, deepLink, match, suggest, listenbrainz, the Zod schemas) is pure and tested; canvas drawing is verified by looking at it. No end-to-end browser tests in v1 because they would mostly assert that a canvas painted something.

nodes.label: Raw Listens Fallback (stats pipeline lag)
nodes.rationale: A real 74,489-listen account (aakash-tir) got 204 from every stats range because ListenBrainz's stats batch job had not run in 5+ weeks (a long-established account's stats carried last_updated 2026-07-05) - the research doc's 'within a day' assumption was too optimistic. Fallback: page /1/user/{name}/listens (up to 3x1000 newest) and rank artists client-side via the pure topArtistsFromListens. mbid_mapping.artists[].artist_mbid is the dataset's own primary key so matching stays exact; an mbid or Spotify id is kept only when all of an artist's listens agree on it, so name collisions degrade to name matching instead of crediting the wrong artist. Architecture unchanged - no diagram update needed.

nodes.label: Song Rows Link Out to Spotify and Deezer
nodes.rationale: Song rows had a <Links> element from the start but Track.links is emitted empty (deferred out of milestone 4), so songs were the one thing on the panel you could not click through. Added the pure, unit-tested src/lib/trackLinks.ts and wired it into DetailPanel's track rows, rendering the links in the same place artist rows already put theirs, right after the listen count. Derived links yield to any real dataset link so a future pipeline that bakes track links takes over silently. Verified in the running app via a headless DOM dump: Unicode titles encode correctly and both generated URL shapes return 200. Architecture unchanged (plain anchors, no new service or runtime call).
nodes.norm_label: song rows link out to spotify and deezer

nodes.label: Exact Spotify Link Probe (MusicBrainz url-rels + Odesli)
nodes.rationale: Evidence behind the search-link choice, probed live before settling. MusicBrainz recording/{mbid}?inc=url-rels returned ZERO url relations for four real dataset tracks (artist-level ~68%, recording-level ~0), so a per-recording pass would add ~9,000 requests at 1 req/s to buy almost nothing. Odesli/song.link - the obvious free Deezer-to-Spotify bridge - resolves a Deezer track to Amazon, Tidal, Napster, Anghami, Boomplay and Yandex while omitting Spotify entirely, confirmed against Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky' and cross-checked by feeding it a Spotify URL (it echoes Spotify back, so it only ever passes the input through). Conclusion: an exact per-song Spotify URL needs the authenticated Spotify API, which the no-keys rule forbids. Deezer is exact for free because the id is already in the dataset.
nodes.norm_label: exact spotify link probe (musicbrainz url-rels + odesli)

nodes.label: Spotify Owner Mode Removal
nodes.rationale: Deleted spotifyAuth.ts, spotifyClient.ts and their test, the owner-mode disclosure in PersonalPanel.tsx, token state in storage.ts, the OAuth callback in usePersonal.ts, the VITE_SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID bake in deploy-pages.yml, and the spotify-personal-mode runbook; the ListenBrainz username path is now the only intake. The owner never registered the Spotify app, so the path was unreachable by anyone, and dev-mode policy capped it at 5 allowlisted users regardless. The matching layer keeps its Spotify-id key because the ListenBrainz intake also supplies Spotify ids from listen metadata, and the dataset's outbound Spotify links are unrelated (they come from MusicBrainz). Stored v2 localStorage values fail the Zod parse and degrade to 'not connected' as designed. Architecture changed, so a diagram update was due.

nodes.label: Post-Merge Chores for PR #35 (graph refresh + diagram)
nodes.rationale: The owner-mode removal dropped an external service and its flows, so the architecture diagram genuinely changed: the 'Spotify (owner)' box is gone, the dashed RUNTIME EXCEPTION group narrows from 332px to 176px to wrap only ListenBrainz, and the lens sublabel drops PKCE for listenbrainz.ts. The graph refresh went 678 to 603 nodes and tripped graphify's shrink guard; rather than force past it blind, old and new node sets were diffed by source file (33 nodes from four deleted files, plus storage.ts -8, vite-env.d.ts -2, usePersonal.ts -1 correctly losing Spotify symbols; edges actually rose 1141 to 1205) before force=True was used. Health diagnostic clean. graphify-out/.graphify_python is now gitignored because it stores an absolute path to this machine's interpreter.
nodes.norm_label: post-merge chores for pr #35 (graph refresh + diagram)
